learningObjectives: Compare All combinations, Orthogonal, Pairwise, Linear expansion and the relation-aware variant.
Calculate simple unconstrained generated-data counts without confusing them with executable TestCases.
Generate combinations at TestSheet, Class or Attribute level and identify the StraightThrough prerequisite.
Separate arranging, duplicate merging and view toggles.

elements.description: Generates the product of defined value choices. Independent unconstrained example: three Attributes with three choices yield 27 datasets. Generated combinations are design Instances, not already executed TestCases.

Uses every defined value at least once while keeping the combination set small. Independent unconstrained example: three Attributes with four choices can cover all values in four rows; this is value coverage, not all pair coverage.
Covers every value pair between two Attributes. This is stronger interaction coverage than merely using every value once, but does not establish full higher-order coverage.

Starts with a defined StraightThrough baseline and varies one non-baseline value per row. In a simple model with one baseline choice per Attribute and nine alternate values in total, this gives ten datasets. The relation-aware variant can add, exclude or constrain combinations.

bulletPoints: Choose coverage deliberately: all value tuples, individual values, value pairs or one-factor variations around a baseline.
Fewer datasets do not guarantee faster execution or easier diagnosis; test implementation and dependencies also matter.

elements.description: The current documentation offers methods for different project needs; it does not establish a universal default or an industry-wide legal mandate. Select a method based on specified coverage, business dependencies and applicable project constraints.

bulletPoints: Linear expansion needs a StraightThrough path. Relations can constrain combinations; assess those rules separately from the simple arithmetic examples.

elements.description: Right-click a TestSheet, TestCase-Design Class or Attribute and select Generate Instances, then the desired method. These design combinations can later support TestCase organization and template instantiation.

elements.term: Combining at Attribute level vs TestSheet level
elements.description: You can generate on a selected Attribute or a TestSheet, and can select particular Attributes or Instances. Confirm the generated values in the selected scope rather than assuming a particular highlight color proves coverage.

elements.text: You must be focused on a particular level (TestSheet or a specific Attribute) to see that level's Instance columns.

bulletPoints: Complete Instances incorporates uncombined values without creating duplicates; it is different from deleting and regenerating an entire collection.

elements.description: Optimize Instances → Arrange Instances arranges the selected Attribute’s Instances; the dynamic-menu reference documents Ctrl+R. The accessed reference does not specify the earlier lesson’s exact five-category sort order.
Merge Instance Duplicates merges duplicates with matching values, Character and Position. Matching display names or values alone do not establish every property is identical.

elements.text: Inspect Instance Usage to see how often a value participates in combinations; adding that column changes the view, not the dataset.
The keyboard reference lists F9 for Show or hide, including Instances. F12 separately shows/hides TestCase-Design instance symbols. Shortcuts apply to the active window.
Independent notes based on current public documentation. Authenticated Academy video/exercises and their numbering were not inspected.

bulletPoints: Arrange reorders; Merge checks duplicate properties; Show/hide changes visibility. None of those actions substitutes for an executed coverage check.

examPitfalls.title: Calculating Orthogonal combinations by multiplying Instance counts
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Using the All Combinations formula (multiplying every Attribute's Instance count together) when asked for the Orthogonal result.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: In the simple unconstrained example, four rows can cover four choices from each Attribute. All combinations instead multiplies the counts; Orthogonal does not imply all value pairs were tested.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming Linear Expansion produces the fewest TestCases
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Confusing Linear Expansion's 'moderate, focused' result set with Orthogonal's 'minimum count' result set.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Compare the coverage goal, not only the count. Linear expansion needs a baseline and varies one alternative at a time; it can miss interacting non-baseline values.

examPitfalls.title: Building Linear Expansion combinations without marking a StraightThrough first
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Generating combinations before any Instance has been flagged as StraightThrough.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Linear Expansion needs a defined StraightThrough baseline before combining — without it, there's no 'happy path' TestCase to expand outward from.

examPitfalls.title: Thinking F9 deletes Instances
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Pressing F9 to 'clean up' a busy TestSheet and assuming the Instances are gone.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: F9 is documented as Show or hide; F12 toggles instance symbols. Neither is the Delete command, and shortcut scope depends on the active window.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An unconstrained design has 3 Attributes, each with 4 choices. How many datasets does All combinations generate?
practiceQuiz.hint: All Combinations multiplies every Attribute's Instance count together.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Each of four choices can accompany each choice in the other two Attributes: 4 × 4 × 4 = 64 datasets. They still need executable tests or template instantiation before a run.

optionExplanations.A: Four rows cover only individual choices in this model, not all tuples.
optionExplanations.B: Adding three counts does not enumerate their cross product.
optionExplanations.C: Four choices in each of three dimensions give 64 tuples.
optionExplanations.D: Seven is not this full-product count.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the same unconstrained design (3 Attributes with 4 choices each), what minimum row count can use every value at least once, as the Orthogonal method requires?
practiceQuiz.hint: At least four rows are needed to include four choices of one Attribute.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Four rows can include all four choices from each Attribute in this simple independent model. They do not necessarily cover every pair; 64 is the full-product count.

optionExplanations.A: 64 is the full cross product, more than individual-value coverage needs.
optionExplanations.B: 12 adds the choice counts rather than combining coverage in rows.
optionExplanations.C: Four rows can cover all four values of every independent Attribute.
optionExplanations.D: Three rows cannot include four distinct choices of one Attribute.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An unconstrained Linear expansion model has one StraightThrough choice per Attribute and nine non-baseline choices in total. With no additional relation rules, how many datasets result?

options.text: 10 — the StraightThrough baseline, plus one TestCase per non-StraightThrough Instance.
36 — all combinations of the 4 Attributes and 9 Instances.

practiceQuiz.hint: Include the baseline once, then one row for each alternate choice.
practiceQuiz.rationale: One baseline plus nine one-factor alternatives gives ten datasets under the stated assumptions. Relation rules can change the set, so this count is not a universal rule for every model.

optionExplanations.A: This omits the StraightThrough baseline row.
optionExplanations.B: The stated baseline plus nine alternatives gives ten rows.
optionExplanations.C: The Attribute count alone does not count all alternate values.
optionExplanations.D: Multiplying Attributes by alternatives is not linear expansion.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which distinction between Arrange Instances and Merge Instance Duplicates matches the documentation?

options.text: Arrange deletes all duplicate values; Merge only changes colors.
Arrange orders Instances; Merge combines duplicates with matching values, Character and Position.
Both commands execute every generated TestCase.

practiceQuiz.hint: Ordering, duplicate consolidation and execution are different actions.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The menu documents arranging Instances; the Instances reference says duplicate merging requires identical values and Character/Position. Neither command executes TestCases.

optionExplanations.A: Ordering and merging are reversed and color is not duplicate identity.
optionExplanations.B: The documented commands distinguish ordering from property-aware duplicate merging.
optionExplanations.C: The reference does not describe deletion of Boundary values by arranging.
optionExplanations.D: Design optimization commands are not test execution.

practiceQuiz.scenario: With TestCase-Design active, a tester uses the documented F9 Show or hide action and Instances disappear from view. Which interpretation is correct?

options.text: All Instances and their combinations were permanently deleted.
The Instance rows were merged as duplicates.
The Instance rows were only hidden from the current view; pressing F9 again reveals them.
The TestSheet was converted into a Class.

practiceQuiz.hint: This is a view toggle, not a data operation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The shortcut changes visibility rather than deleting data or changing object types. F12 is the separate instance-symbol visibility action. Verify the active window when using shortcuts.

optionExplanations.A: Show or hide does not permanently delete Instances.
optionExplanations.B: Merging is a separate optimization command.
optionExplanations.C: F9 changes visibility; the underlying data remains.
optionExplanations.D: Object conversion is a separate command.

quickRecap.value: Full product in an unconstrained design; generated datasets still need executable tests.
Individual-value coverage; not the same as pair coverage.
Covers each value pair across two Attributes, not every higher-order interaction.
One baseline plus one-factor alternatives in the simple model; relation-aware expansion can alter combinations.
Arranges Instances (Ctrl+R); exact historical sort ordering not verified.
Merge duplicates with identical values, Character and Position.
F9: Show or hide. F12: instance-symbol visibility. Active-window context matters.
